context_requirements: Cells must express farnesyltransferase (FNTA/FNTB) and have farnesylated proteins whose function is required for proliferation or survival.
Cells with mutant RAS may be less sensitive because KRAS and NRAS can be geranylgeranylated when farnesylation is blocked.
Responsive lines should have intact sterol regulatory element-binding protein (SREBP) signaling to mount a compensatory cholesterol synthesis response.
falsifiers: No change in cholesterol synthesis genes (e.g., HMGCR, HMGCS1, FDFT1) at 24 h in any cell line.
No decrease in proliferation or G1 arrest at 24 h in any cell line.
Strong and consistent upregulation of generic stress markers (e.g., HSPA1A, DNAJB1) at 6 h across all lines, which would suggest nonspecific toxicity rather than FTI-specific effects.
Greater sensitivity in KRAS-mutant lines (A549, HEPG2, HCT116-like) than in KRAS-wild-type lines, contradicting the known resistance of KRAS-driven cells to FTIs.
